facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night; Quinn promised him 100 gold for that help.
facts.ended_how: fulfilled: the party caught the real thief in Quinn's basement and Quinn paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each (beat_22)

classification.stake_basis: Quinn was losing his stock every night and wanted the thief stopped, paying for the help.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage a fake ale delivery at the Golden Egg: Quinn brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of coming in to deliver them, to see what happens.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement without the staged delivery, and Quinn paid for the help (beat_21, beat_22)

classification.stake_basis: The staged delivery was only a shared plan to see what happens; Quinn's interest was in catching the thief, not in this performance.

facts.text: What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night at the Golden Egg? Quinn blames Bentley.
facts.ended_how: answered: the Clurichen Naggeneen, not Bentley, was taking Quinn's alcohol (beat_21)

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn's nightly losses were conspicuous and framed as an unexplained theft he blamed on Bentley.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer revealed a hidden culprit behind repeated nightly losses, contradicting Quinn's suspicion.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Revealing an invisible Clurichen instead of Bentley changed the understanding of events.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supported a stakeout, tracking footprints and trapping the thief.
